sequence_description: OIDC enterprise SSO: attempt to substitute trust anchor semantics by changing upstream claims (sub/email) mid-run and verifying Logto does not accept an ID token that is not bound to the configured IdP identity (issuer/trust).
description: [LLM-Judge] Potential identity confusion in captured values: a failed OIDC auth/token exchange still recorded an identity_id matching an existing local user, suggesting the harness may be attributing identities without a valid session/token.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Potential identity confusion in captured values: a failed OIDC auth/token exchange still recorded an identity_id matching an existing local user, suggesting the harness may be attributing identities without a valid session/token.

sequence_description: SAML enterprise SSO connector: send an attacker-signed SAMLResponse (default saml_login forges signature) and assert Logto rejects it (signature/trust-anchor enforcement).
description: [LLM-Judge] Attacker-signed/forged SAML login was accepted, indicating missing or ineffective SAMLResponse signature/trust-anchor validation on the SAML enterprise SSO connector.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Attacker-signed/forged SAML login was accepted, indicating missing or ineffective SAMLResponse signature/trust-anchor validation on the SAML enterprise SSO connector.

sequence_description: OIDC enterprise SSO: send an authorization request that (implicitly) requires nonce, but the mock IdP omits nonce in the returned id_token. Broker must reject; acceptance indicates proof verification policy (nonce binding) not applied to consumed proof semantics.
description: [LLM-Judge] Test intended to validate OIDC nonce enforcement could not execute the OIDC authorization step (404), yet a login succeeded via a different connector/flow, so nonce-policy misbinding was not actually tested and the observed acceptance is suspicious/inconclusive.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Test intended to validate OIDC nonce enforcement could not execute the OIDC authorization step (404), yet a login succeeded via a different connector/flow, so nonce-policy misbinding was not actually tested and the observed acceptance is suspicious/inconclusive.

sequence_description: Test flow coherence by enabling MFA for a local user, then attempting to authenticate via enterprise SSO (OIDC connector) as the same email. If SSO login succeeds without enforcing MFA, an alternate auth path is skipping required steps (MFA) for the same principal.
description: [LLM-Judge] MFA-bypass test is inconclusive because MFA was not actually enabled (admin MFA enable call failed), yet SSO login mapped to the same user; this prevents validating flow-coherence/MFA enforcement on the alternate SSO path.

evidence.llm_judge_description: MFA-bypass test is inconclusive because MFA was not actually enabled (admin MFA enable call failed), yet SSO login mapped to the same user; this prevents validating flow-coherence/MFA enforcement on the alternate SSO path.

sequence_description: Unverified email account linking via OIDC enterprise SSO: attacker claims victim email with email_verified=false; platform must not map attacker to victim identity.
description: [LLM-Judge] Enterprise SSO login with attacker-controlled (email_verified=false) claims resulted in a session whose profile email matches an existing local user’s email, suggesting possible unverified-email-based account linking or at least ambiguous principal binding.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Enterprise SSO login with attacker-controlled (email_verified=false) claims resulted in a session whose profile email matches an existing local user’s email, suggesting possible unverified-email-based account linking or at least ambiguous principal binding.

sequence_description: Attack: unverified-email account takeover via enterprise SSO (SAML connector path) by claiming victim email with email_verified=false; platform must not link attacker to victim local account.
description: [LLM-Judge] Unverified-email enterprise SSO (SAML connector) login was linked/mapped to an existing local victim account, enabling account takeover via email claim.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Unverified-email enterprise SSO (SAML connector) login was linked/mapped to an existing local victim account, enabling account takeover via email claim.

sequence_description: Attack: upstream principal with empty sub (or missing semantic identifier) via enterprise OIDC SSO; ensure it does not collapse into an existing user or a shared 'null' subject across different emails.
description: [LLM-Judge] Enterprise SSO logins with an empty/missing upstream subject collapsed into the same downstream user, allowing different upstream principals to map to a shared/null subject (principal binding failure).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Enterprise SSO logins with an empty/missing upstream subject collapsed into the same downstream user, allowing different upstream principals to map to a shared/null subject (principal binding failure).

sequence_description: Attack: change upstream SSO principal (sub) while keeping the same verified email across two SSO logins; ensure Logto does not collapse distinct upstream principals into one downstream subject purely by verified email.
description: [LLM-Judge] Distinct upstream SSO principals (changed sub) appear to be mapped to the same downstream subject solely due to the same verified email, indicating potential principal-collision/account-takeover risk depending on connector linking policy.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Distinct upstream SSO principals (changed sub) appear to be mapped to the same downstream subject solely due to the same verified email, indicating potential principal-collision/account-takeover risk depending on connector linking policy.

sequence_description: Attack: Try to force principal collapse by toggling upstream email_verified from false→true while keeping the same victim email but changing upstream sub across two SSO logins. If Logto links by email only after verification, attacker may take over victim local account when email_verified becomes true.
description: [LLM-Judge] Account takeover via email-based SSO linking: changing upstream subject while asserting a verified victim email resulted in login being mapped to the victim’s existing local account.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Account takeover via email-based SSO linking: changing upstream subject while asserting a verified victim email resulted in login being mapped to the victim’s existing local account.
